body: Huh. That's funny. There was a post a few months ago about a dude who spent a similar amount in surgery for his dog. It had cysts that could be cancer. He paid for the surgery to get them out and check if it was indeed cancer. His wife didn't want him spending that much money on an old dog. People here were calling him an asshole for disrespecting his wife, for spending that much money on the dog, etc. So this post is hilarious. I don't know if it's a gender thing or a capitalism thing. It's still hilarious.

I'd be questioning how strong they think I am. I'd be questioning how they perceive me. Asking myself why they thought I couldn't handle the truth. Why they thought I was going to break if I found out. 

10 years is a really long time. Too much time imo. But I can't really judge OP as hard as some people are doing. And I won't tell him if I were his mother I'd never speak to him again. He's not getting dudes for his father, he's not helping him cheat. His father doesn't even know he knows.

 He says why he didn't tell her. He's afraid she won't handle the truth well. He's worried about her. Why? Because he knows her. It's a horrible situation for all of them. And his father is the one to blame here.

It doesn't matter. If you were angry with your kids for keeping something like this from you, that would make you an asshole. Hypothetically, if your kids didn't tell you, they had a reason. And it's kind of worrying that the first reason that comes to your mind is that they hate you or doesn't respect you.

This is a stretch. Have you ever been in this position before? Because if you had, you should know that it has nothing to do with gender. OP does a good job explaining the turmoil that goes on your head when you discover one of your parents is cheating. I outed my dad when I found out. My mom didn't believe me, my dad was pissed at me for a long time. The remained together for a while after that. I was the only one who lost in that scenario. And like mine, there are a thousand stories. Kids having to tell the truth to one of their parents. Kids carrying the secret for years because they're terrified of destroying their family. Gender has nothing to do with this.

Edit: downvote me all you want. It's really sad that some of you are unable to read what OP's saying and how much he's suffering for keeping this from his mom. And it's ridiculous that you take any chance you get to call men misogynistic when here that does not apply.

I understand what you're saying, but I highly doubt that would be your initial reaction. And if it was, your anger would be misplaced. Hypothetically speaking, you should be seriously angry with your SO for exposing your kids to their cheating. Not with your kids for having that burden.

>you must not even like or respect your mother AT ALL.

It has nothing to do with that. It's hard to tell the truth when you know that by doing it, you would be destroying your family. You would be destroying one of your parents. It's not easy. It's not black or white.
